title: S3.7c canonical ACIS cylinder-surface projection and signed distance

scope.geometry: Closest point and signed radial distance on the untrimmed circular-cylinder locus represented by the canonical cone-surface profile
scope.domain: Finite decoded cone-surface face with ratio=1, sineAngle=0, cosineAngle=1, finite origin/axis/major-axis, nonzero axis, and positive representable major-axis magnitude
scope.projection_policy: Project the query onto the axis line through the decoded origin and add the decoded major-axis magnitude along the normalized radial query direction
scope.ambiguity_policy: Refuse points whose radial component is zero or within a small floating-point roundoff floor of the axis; for exactly coordinate-aligned axes, preserve nonzero representable perpendicular components when both perpendicular point-origin differences are finite, rather than comparing them with the axial magnitude; leave caller output unchanged
scope.numeric_policy: Scale axis/radius and point-origin arithmetic; preserve tiny representable radii when their normalized fraction underflows; for exact coordinate-aligned axes, derive radial direction/distance from the two perpendicular point-origin differences even if the axial difference overflows; refuse unrepresentable final coordinates
scope.reference_scope: Versioned ACadRust 0.5.5 docs.rs source documents the cylinder angle profile and writer radius convention; the newer release/source identity mismatch remains unresolved, so this is implementation corroboration only, not normative ACIS semantics
non_claims: cylinder parameterization, face orientation, UV trims, or pcurve evaluation
native consumer or independent-kernel semantic qualification

source.reference_reviewed: The versioned 0.5.5 writer documents cos_half_angle=1 and sin_half_angle=0 for its cylinder profile and derives the reference cross-section radius from the major-axis vector magnitude. The plan notes a newer v0.6.5 release/source identity discrepancy, so this supports only the bounded implementation profile selected here; it is not an independent ACIS semantic oracle.
